task_meta.instruction:
The apps for this task are already open in separate browser tabs and logged in. Just switch between these tabs to do the task -- no sign-in or URL needed.

Your Gmail inbox holds the overnight payment alerts from the billing system (from 'Billing System'). Each alert names one customer, an amount, and (for payment receipts) an invoice number. Work through every alert email and take the corrective action that its alert type calls for, but ONLY when the item is not already in the target state (verify current state first and skip anything already resolved):
- 'Duplicate charge': refund the matching Stripe payment (match by customer and amount). If that payment has already been refunded, leave it alone.
- 'Chargeback opened': in Stripe, submit dispute evidence on the matching dispute for that customer so it moves out of the needs-response state. If the dispute is no longer awaiting a response, leave it alone.
- 'Payment received': in QuickBooks, record payment on the invoice whose number is in the alert so it becomes Paid. If it is already Paid, leave it alone.
- 'Under investigation': do NOT act on these alerts -- they are pending and must be left untouched.
Skip any alert whose customer has no matching Stripe payment/dispute or QuickBooks invoice.

For every alert you actually acted on: in Gmail, apply the matching status label to that alert email -- 'Refunded' for a refund, 'Disputed' for a chargeback, 'Reconciled' for a recorded payment -- and reply to the customer (their email address is in the alert). Do not label or reply to alerts you left untouched or skipped.

When you have handled every actionable alert, post a one-line summary of the cleanup (including how many alerts you resolved) to the Slack '#billing-ops' channel and pin that message.

A message action context menu is open on the right side of the message, listing options from top to bottom: Edit message, Bookmark message, Pin to channel, Copy message link, Copy text, and Delete message. The message composition area is visible at the bottom of the channel.

planner_layer.intent: Enter edit mode for the posted summary message so the duplicated text can be corrected.
planner_layer.thought: The summary message that was posted contains an obvious duplication—the entire sentence repeats twice. The message action menu is already open, and selecting 'Edit message' will open the message in an inline editor so I can remove the duplicate portion and save a clean summary.
planner_layer.expectation: The context menu will close and the message will transform into an editable text field pre-filled with the current text, accompanied by Cancel and Save Changes buttons.

executor_layer.action_description: In order to correct the duplicated text in the posted summary, I need to click the 'Edit message' option in the message action menu.

validation_layer.post_verification_rule: The message must enter edit mode: the context menu disappears, the message text appears inside an editable input field, and 'Cancel' and 'Save Changes' buttons appear below it.
validation_layer.reflection: The context menu is no longer visible. The message text is now displayed inside an editable text box, and below it are 'Cancel' and 'Save Changes' buttons, along with the hint 'Escape to cancel · Enter to save'. This confirms the action successfully entered message edit mode.

value.observation: The screen shows a Slack Clone workspace in the '#billing-ops' channel. A message from Dana Reyes is open in edit mode. planner_layer.intent: Replace the duplicated summary text in the message editor with a single correct instance so the message can be saved properly.

To fix this, all text in the edit field must be selected and then overwritten with the correct single version of the summary. executor_layer.action_description: In order to replace the duplicated summary with the correct single version, I need to click inside the message edit area to focus it, select all existing text with Ctrl+A, and paste the correct summary text from the clipboard to overwrite the selection.

validation_layer.post_verification_rule: The edit field must contain exactly one non-duplicated instance of the summary sentence, and the 'Save Changes' button must appear active (green/highlighted) instead of gray.
validation_layer.reflection: Comparing the before and after screens, the duplicated text has been successfully replaced with a single correct instance of the summary. The 'Save Changes' button has changed from gray to green, confirming the edit field now holds modified content ready to be saved.
